subtasks.description:
Add View() rendering tests to agents_test.go that verify context percentage appears inline on the activity metrics line rather than on its own separate line.

Test cases:
1. Agent with both activity data and ctx%: output should contain a single line matching '▸ Read foo | 3/5 files | no commit | ctx: 85%' — the ctx portion must be on the SAME line as the tool/target, not a separate line. Verify the output does NOT contain a standalone '    ctx: 85%' line.
2. Agent with ctx% but NO activity data: ctx% should still appear as a standalone detail line (fallback behavior, e.g., '    ctx: 50%').
3. Agent with activity data but NO ctx%: activity line should render normally without ctx suffix.
4. Ctx% at warning threshold (>=75): verify the rendered line contains 'ctx: 75%' inline with activity.
5. Ctx% at danger threshold (>=90): verify the rendered line contains 'ctx: 95%' inline with activity.
6. Scroll block height: an agent with BOTH activity and ctx% should produce the same number of output lines as an agent with activity but no ctx%. This proves ctx no longer adds a separate line when activity is present.

Color rendering detail: since the activity line uses phase-based colors and ctx uses threshold-based colors, the implementation will render the ctx suffix as a separately-styled string concatenated to the activity string. Tests should verify the ctx text appears on the activity line by checking that '| ctx: N%' appears in the line starting with '▸'.

The tests call View() on an AgentsModel with crafted agents and check the output string. Tests will initially FAIL because ctx is still rendered on a separate line.

IMPORTANT: Use a helper like ptr() for uuid pointers — it already exists in agents_test.go (check for existing helper at bottom of file, or in testutil). Set width to a large value (e.g., 120) so truncation doesn't interfere.

subtasks.description:
Modify the View() method in agents.go to render context percentage inline on the activity line instead of as a separate line.

Detailed changes to internal/tui/agents.go View() method:

1. REMOVE the standalone ctx block (current lines 153-166) that appends a separate '    ctx: N%' line.

2. In the activity line rendering section (current lines 177-220):
   a. After building actLine with tool/target/progress/committed (line ~201), check if context_used_pct exists in ag.Config.
   b. If it exists, build a ctx suffix string like ' | ctx: N%'.
   c. Determine the ctx style based on thresholds (>=90 danger, >=75 warning, else subtitleStyle).
   d. Render the activity portion with actStyle and the ctx suffix with ctxStyle, then concatenate them into one line before appending to lines.
   e. The concatenation approach: `actStyle.Render(actLine) + ctxStyle.Render(ctxSuffix)` — this produces a single string with mixed ANSI colors on one line.

3. ADD a fallback block AFTER the activity section: if there was NO activity line but context_used_pct exists, render ctx on its own standalone line (same as current behavior). This handles agents that have ctx data but haven't started any tool activity yet.

4. UPDATE the scroll block height calculation (current lines 229-254):
   - When activity is present, do NOT count ctx as a separate line (it's now part of the activity line).
   - When activity is absent but ctx exists, still count it as a line.
   - The logic: `hasActivity && hasCTX` = no extra line for ctx. `!hasActivity && hasCTX` = +1 line for ctx.

The implementation must make the pre-written tests pass without modifying them.

Final integration verification:
1. Run all TUI tests (`go test ./internal/tui/...`) to confirm nothing is broken.
2. Verify the change works correctly with the scroll calculation — no off-by-one in agent block heights.
3. Check if README.md describes the TUI ctx display format. If it does, update it to reflect that ctx% now appears inline on the activity metrics line. If README doesn't mention ctx display, no update needed.

This subtask is simple integration wiring — the feature is a single-file UI change with no cross-package dependencies.
